title: Full-Stack Capstone Exam
description: The final boss. Review everything from responsive web design, JavaScript, frontend development libraries, Python, relational databases, and backend development & APIs before taking the 50-question full-stack exam.

sections.title: Responsive Web Design Review
sections.content: Responsive web design makes websites adapt to different screen sizes and devices. A mobile-first approach starts by designing for smaller screens and then adding styles for larger screens. The viewport meta tag helps browsers display pages correctly on mobile devices. Media queries apply CSS rules at specific conditions such as screen width. Flexible units such as vw and rem, along with Flexbox and Grid, help create layouts that adapt to different screen sizes.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of responsive web design?
choices: To make a website adapt to different screen sizes
To make every website use the same font
To prevent websites from working on mobile devices
To remove CSS from a website

quiz.question: What does the viewport meta tag help control?
choices: How a page is scaled and displayed on mobile devices

quiz.question: Which CSS feature can apply styles based on screen width?

sections.title: JavaScript Fundamentals Review
sections.content: JavaScript adds programming logic and interactivity to web applications. Variables store values, with let used when a variable may be reassigned and const used when it should not be reassigned. Functions group reusable instructions and can accept parameters and return values. Arrays store multiple values in an ordered collection and use zero-based indexing, meaning the first item is at index 0.
examples: function add(a, b) { return a + b; }

quiz.question: Which JavaScript keyword declares a variable that can be reassigned?
What is a parameter in a function?
choices: A value or variable received by the function

quiz.question: What index represents the first item in a JavaScript array?

sections.title: Frontend Development Libraries Review
sections.content: Component-based frontend libraries organize user interfaces into reusable components. Components can receive read-only data from parents through props. State represents data managed by a component that can change over time. Hooks provide features that allow function components to use capabilities such as state. The useState Hook provides a current state value and an updater function. Updating state can cause the component to render again with the new value.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of components in a component-based UI?
choices: To create reusable pieces of a user interface

quiz.question: What are props used for?
choices: Passing read-only data from a parent to a component

quiz.question: What does useState provide?
choices: A state value and an updater function

sections.title: Python Fundamentals Review
sections.content: Python is a dynamically typed programming language. Variables can store values such as integers, floats, strings, and booleans without requiring an explicit type declaration. Control flow uses if, elif, and else for decisions, while for and while loops repeat instructions. Python uses indentation to define code blocks. Functions are created with def, can accept parameters, and can return values using return.

sections.title: Relational Databases Review
sections.content: A relational database organizes data into tables containing rows and columns. A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table, while a foreign key connects a row to a related row in another table. SQL SELECT retrieves data, and WHERE filters which rows are returned. JOIN combines related data from multiple tables. GROUP BY organizes rows into groups, while aggregate functions such as COUNT(), SUM(), and AVG() calculate values from groups or sets of rows.
examples: SELECT customers.name, orders.id FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;
SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;

quiz.question: What uniquely identifies a row in a relational table?
What does the WHERE clause do in a SELECT query?
choices: Filters rows based on a condition

quiz.question: What does COUNT() do in SQL?

sections.title: Backend Development & APIs Review
sections.content: Backend applications process requests from clients and return responses. HTTP provides methods such as GET for retrieving data, POST for creating data, PUT or PATCH for updating data, and DELETE for removing data. REST APIs expose resources through predictable URLs and commonly return structured JSON data. HTTP status codes communicate results, including 200 for success, 201 for creation, 400 for a bad request, 401 for unauthorized access, 404 for a missing resource, and 500 for a server error. Authentication, such as authentication tokens, helps confirm who is making a request.
